summary: A Network Host Status report covering April 24 to May 5, 1972. The USC IBM 360/44 became a network user during that time. It updates RFC 332. It was replaced by RFC 344.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 342 reports daily ARPANET host tests from April 24 to May 5, 1972. It records the USC IBM 360/44 becoming a network user and explains the status codes used in its tables.

questions: which arpanet hosts were tested in rfc 342
subtitle: A Network Host Status report covering April 24 through May 5, 1972.

tldr.problem: ARPANET users needed current information on host availability and which machines were servers or users.
tldr.mechanism: The report gives daily host test results and a separate table of host status or predictions for April 24 through May 5.
tldr.outcome: RFC 342 updates RFC 332 and was later obsoleted by RFC 344; it notes that the USC IBM 360/44 became a network user.

facts.label: Status codes
facts.value: O, D, H, T, R, F

today: RFC 342 updates RFC 332 and was later obsoleted by RFC 344.

sections.title: Report Period and Host Categories
sections.content:
RFC 342 reports the status of most Network Hosts from April 24 to May 5. During that period, the IBM 360/44 at the University of Southern California, Network Address 23, became a Network user.

Hosts not expected to function regularly as servers for at least two weeks were excluded from daily testing. The report also excludes hosts intended to be users only, including Terminal IMPs and the Network Control Center computer used to gather network statistics.
sections.plainLanguage: The report tracks host tests over a defined period and notes one new network user at USC. It leaves out hosts not expected to serve other sites and hosts intended only as users.

sections.title: Daily Test Codes
sections.content:
The daily table uses six codes: O (Open), D (Dead), H (Half Open), T (Timed out), R (Refused), and F (Full). Full means a host opened a connection, reported that all Network ports were in use, and immediately closed the connection.

A timeout means the destination did not complete the ICP and open a connection within 60 seconds. The tables also mark sites that warned they might be unavailable at certain times.
sections.plainLanguage: The codes describe how each host responded. F means it opened a connection but said all network ports were in use; T means it did not open within 60 seconds.

sections.title: Reported Host Status
sections.content:
A second table lists sites, computers, reported status or predictions, and the person who provided each report. The table distinguishes server hosts from user-only systems and includes descriptions such as Server (Experimental), User Now, and Soon.

The document says the USC IBM 360/44 became a Network user during the reporting period. Its test results and the status table are separate forms of information in the report.
sections.plainLanguage: The report includes both measured test results and people's reports about each host's role. It identifies the USC IBM 360/44 as a new network user.
